section: Arab conquest of Sindh (712 CE); Ghaznavid and Ghurid invasions - Mahmud, Muhammad Ghori, Battles of Tarain

accepted.s: Somnath Swabhiman Parv was launched in January 2026 to commemorate which historical event?
o: Muhammad Ghori's victory in the Battle of Chandawar
Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath, a thousand years earlier
The Arab conquest of Sindh by Muhammad bin Qasim
accepted.x: Somnath Swabhiman Parv was launched in January 2026 to mark 1,000 years since Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive event-year association and distinguish the commemoration from other invasions.

accepted.s: Which event is regarded as the turning point for the establishment of Turkish rule in North India?
o: The Arab conquest of Sindh in 712 CE
Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath
The Second Battle of Tarain in 1192
accepted.x: The Second Battle of Tarain, fought in 1192, is regarded as the turning point that enabled the establishment of Turkish rule in North India.
accepted.tq: Identify the decisive event by separating a turning point from earlier raids and subsequent consolidation.

accepted.s: The principal historical significance of the Arab contact with India beginning in 712 CE was that it
o: ended all indigenous scientific traditions in India
caused the immediate conversion of all Indian rulers to Islam
established permanent Arab rule over the whole of North India
accepted.x: The Arab contact beginning with the conquest of Sindh in 712 CE helped Indian scientific knowledge move westward and subsequently reach the Islamic world and Europe.
accepted.tq: Select the precise consequence and reject extreme claims about political or religious transformation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the objectives of Mahmud of Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori in India?
o: Mahmud mainly raided for plunder, whereas Ghori aimed at conquest and permanent occupation.
Mahmud sought territorial consolidation, whereas Ghori conducted raids for plunder.
Both Mahmud and Ghori were primarily interested only in religious conversion.
Both Mahmud and Ghori confined their activities to the conquest of Sindh.
accepted.x: Mahmud of Ghazni is characterised mainly as a plunder-seeking raider, while Muhammad Ghori pursued conquest and established a lasting political presence in North India.
accepted.tq: Split the options by comparing the motive and long-term objective of the two invaders.
